primitives.name: Punt Return Positioning
primitives.verbatim_quote: INDIVIDUAL POSITIONS 125 When his own side punts, it is the duty of the end to get down the field with the ball to prevent a return run.
primitives.assumptions: Linear field traversal, constant end speed, deterministic ball trajectory.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Ball catch occurs before end arrival.

layer2.mapping: State-space evolution of end position relative to ball and opposing blocker using kinematic constraints.

primitives.name: Blocking Avoidance Strategy
primitives.verbatim_quote: In doing this, if the opposing end is blocking on the line of scrimmage, it is better that the end start from his position close to tackle, and go directly down the field, taking care to keep outside of the ball and the man who is catching it.
primitives.assumptions: Opposing end acts as static obstacle, linear path assumed.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to obstacle avoidance in control theory with angular margin enforcement.

primitives.name: Ball Fall Prediction
primitives.verbatim_quote: In going down on a punt, the end must determine about where the ball will fall by the general movements of the men in the backfield or by snatching a glimpse at the ball over his shoulder as he runs.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'t_{fall}': 'estimated time to impact (seconds)', 'v_{ball}': 'ball velocity vector (m/s)', 'θ_{view}': 'visual angle of ball (radians)'}
primitives.assumptions: Backfield motion provides predictive signal; visual cue is instantaneous.

layer2.mapping: Kinematic estimation of ball trajectory via multi-source sensory fusion.
layer2.telemetry: Predicted vs actual ball landing point deviation.
